# 2020–2021 INFINITE RECHARGE – hindsight

Source: user hindsight notes, batch 1 (2026-09-27). The season was not fully played; robots were built and played in
offseason events.

## Game play / meta
- **Small top wheels to reduce spin on an extended hood** became a meta that season (used again in 2022 and 2026).
  They were driven from the main flywheel (same motor), smaller in diameter and geared to control the spin.

## Dominant robots
- **1690, 179** – 1690 dominated the season: a spindexer with a collapsible shooter to fit under the control panel
  ("spinner"). They also used the extending shooter for a high release point, so they could shoot at a high
  percentage from the closer safe zone into the inner port. 179 looked like a good concept but did not play the
  season. 1690 liked to steal balls from the opponents' overflow for short cycles.
- **973** – kept it simple: did not aim to go under the spinner; tall robot (high release, not blocked); did not even
  aim for the inner port. Focused on fast cycles and quick releases.
- **4414** (offseason) – small robot, to avoid defense, with a turret.
- **2910** (offseason) – small robot with active S-shaped funneling using belts (3476 had a similar robot with brushes
  instead of belt funneling).

## Effective mechanisms
- **4414 / 1678** hood with spin minimization.
- **1690 / 148 / 1678** extendable / collapsible shooter.
- **1690 / 1678** spindexer.
- **2481** high-MOI shooter with a bicycle wheel as the flywheel – unique; not clear whether effective, since they did
  not play real competition. Special and creative: the idea was to shoot consistently from far away (behind the
  spinner), even with balls in different wear conditions.
